en-US.name: Impeccable
en-US.summary: A design language that makes AI better at frontend: UX review, visual hierarchy, accessibility, typography, color, motion and reusable design systems. Uses an upstream standalone binary launcher that may download on first run; platform and execution permissions must be supplied separately. Optional image comps can fall back to OpenAI's image API when OPENAI_API_KEY is set, billed to the operator's own account.

zh-CN.name: Impeccable
zh-CN.summary: 让 AI 更懂设计的前端设计语言：覆盖 UX 审查、视觉层级、可访问性、排版、配色、动效与可复用设计系统，把界面打磨到生产级。新版本使用上游独立二进制启动器，可能在首次运行时下载；需自行满足平台与运行权限。可选的图像草图在设置 OPENAI_API_KEY 时可回退调用 OpenAI 图像 API，费用计入运营者自有账户。

requirements.value: Impeccable 4.8.0 runs its standalone launcher and engine binary 0.1.18. If the binary is absent, the launcher downloads it from the upstream GitHub release and refuses it unless its SHA-256 matches the digest in the bundled scripts/engine-checksums.txt; a copy cached under ~/.impeccable (or IMPECCABLE_HOME) is checked the same way before first use. The operator must permit that download and execution. Windows without sh uses the .cmd launcher. DesireCore does not install or operate the binary.

A first-run binary download requires network access to upstream distribution. If the launcher is unavailable, follow the upstream documented direct-context fallback and report that the launcher did not run.

Optional comp-first image generation prefers the host's own image tool. Only when OPENAI_API_KEY is set does the engine's generate-image fallback call api.openai.com, billed to the operator's own OpenAI account; the agent must say so before the first render. DesireCore does not provide or pay for that key.

The optional design-detector hook is written into agent settings (project hook files, or ~/.claude/settings.json for a user-scope Claude install) only when the operator turns it on, and then runs the engine unsandboxed, with the agent's environment and network access, after UI edits; it adds reminders and does not block edits. Desktop-app audits attach to an operator-launched app's local DevTools port; keep it on 127.0.0.1 and prefer test profiles and data.
